The given statements establish a large number of ancestor–descendant chains. By transitive closure these chains merge, and the two individuals of interest can be placed relative to one another as follows.

- Starting from Madison yields the forward chain  
  Madison \(\to\) Harold \(\to\) Jordan \(\to\) Noah \(\to\) Timothy \(\to\) Matthew \(\to\) Mary \(\to\) Janet \(\to\) Katherine \(\to\) Dorothy \(\to\) Brandon \(\to\) Anthony \(\to\) Mason \(\to\) James \(\to\) Karen \(\to\) Brian \(\to\) Lawrence \(\to\) Marie \(\to\) Joan \(\to\) Joyce \(\to\) Melissa \(\to\) Aaron \(\to\) Doris \(\to\) Richard \(\to\) Jose \(\to\) Alexander \(\to\) Andrea \(\to\) Arthur.  
  Consequently Madison is an ancestor of Arthur.

- Starting from Shirley yields a second forward chain that ultimately reaches the same individual:  
  Shirley \(\to\) Evelyn \(\to\) Theresa \(\to\) Peter \(\to\) Barbara \(\to\) Nicole \(\to\) Elijah \(\to\) Kevin \(\to\) Sophia \(\to\) Scott \(\to\) Donald \(\to\) Rachel \(\to\) Austin \(\to\) Douglas \(\to\) Alice \(\to\) Michelle \(\to\) Betty \(\to\) Hannah \(\to\) Daniel \(\to\) Margaret \(\to\) Judy \(\to\) Christina \(\to\) Bradley \(\to\) Ralph \(\to\) Jack \(\to\) Eugene \(\to\) Samantha \(\to\) George \(\to\) Terry \(\to\) Charlotte \(\to\) Carol \(\to\) Patricia \(\to\) Bryan \(\to\) Ryan \(\to\) Amanda \(\to\) Kenneth \(\to\) Arthur.  
  Consequently Shirley is also an ancestor of Arthur.

Arthur is therefore a descendant of both Madison and Shirley; i.e., Madison and Shirley share a common descendant.  

Neither person appears in the descendant list of the other, so neither is an ancestor of the other. No individual is supplied that is an ancestor of both, so they are not known to share a common ancestor. The only relation that is entailed by the given statements is therefore option 4.

<ANSWER>4</ANSWER>
